races.name: Celebrating National Racehorse Week Novices' Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: King's Scholar
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner at OR 123 with back-to-back hurdle wins on Good ground; Tom Hutsby claims 10lb and for a 5yo chasing a hat-trick of sorts, the prominent style should keep him close enough to Whermyrosemarygoes to pounce if she weakens; 86 days off is the only mild query.

runners_data.name: Playful Fox
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton takes the ride for his brother Dan's yard, a powerful combination, and the hold-up style suits a horse whose best finishes (2-1) have come on Good ground over 2m; the closing shape this race presents is modest so she may need to be nudged forward more than usual.

runners_data.name: Bacardi Blue
runners_data.note: Bryan Carver pushes forward in a prominent role from OR 120, but only three runs on similar going (0 wins, 1 place) and form figures of 5-5-2-6-3 suggest she finds her ceiling here; a novice handling Newton Abbot's tight track for the first time is an added unknown.

runners_data.name: Devon Red
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 7yo flagged as unexposed with just one run on similar going; the unknown style (mapped U) and Nick Scholfield's modest T14 record (1/4) make him hard to assess, though a clean jumping round could see him outrun his odds if conditions suit.

runners_data.name: Whermyrosemarygoes
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner, trained by Faye Bramley and ridden by Harry Cobden — a marquee booking that signals stable confidence; her recent win on Good ground over the same 2m trip and an uncontested lead profile make her the dominant tactical force in this race.

runners_data.name: Lundy View
runners_data.note: Consistent tail-ender with four runs on similar going all producing finishes of 6th, 7th or worse; James Davies partners a horse whose hold-up style leaves her reliant on others stopping, and her form trajectory offers little encouragement at this level.

races.paceDynamic: Whermyrosemarygoes is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner novice hurdle and, with no rival willing to dispute the lead, Harry Cobden can dictate a sustainable, uncontested gallop from the front over the 2m1f trip on Good ground at Newton Abbot. King's Scholar and Bacardi Blue will press forward in prominent positions just off the leader, creating a small cluster at the head of affairs, while Playful Fox and Lundy View settle in behind as hold-up types. The overall tempo will be honest but controlled, with Whermyrosemarygoes able to manage the fractions entirely on her own terms — a scenario that historically favours horses racing prominently or from the front, who can avoid getting caught in traffic and attack the final two hurdles with energy in hand. This race shape most clearly favours prominent and front-running profiles, as the uncontested leader sets a tempo that tests hold-up horses' ability to close on a flat, turning track that does not always generate a strong late surge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Whermyrosemarygoes Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Whermyrosemarygoes bowls along at her own pace and the hold-up horses cannot close the gap on the run-in.
scenarios.body: Cobden pings her out, dictates every stride on Good ground, and the modest six-runner field lacks the firepower to reel her in; her recent win at 2m hurdles on Good going and Harry Cobden's big-race front-running nous are the key ingredients. Horses racing prominently — King's Scholar and Bacardi Blue — are best placed to challenge if she falters, but a smooth front-runner can be very hard to catch at Newton Abbot.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Peg Her Back
scenarios.trigger: If King's Scholar or Bacardi Blue push up aggressively early and force a genuine pace, leaving Whermyrosemarygoes vulnerable in the final stages.
scenarios.body: A contested early gallop lifts the tempo and brings a staying test into play over the last half-mile, suiting a horse with class and a turn of foot; King's Scholar's OR of 123 and back-to-back wins on Good ground make him the standout beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Sweep Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that the front-runners tire and Playful Fox or Lundy View can produce a sustained run from the back.
scenarios.body: Harry Skelton's track record on hold-up horses is excellent, and Playful Fox's form figures of 2-1-2 on Good ground suggest she can finish well when the tempo truly stacks up in her favour. However, Newton Abbot's flat finish and small field make a late-closing scenario less likely than in more open races.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Race, Outsider Profits
scenarios.trigger: If interference or jumping errors disrupt the front group and a lightly-raced or rejuvenated runner sneaks a place at a big price.
scenarios.body: Devon Red is lightly raced (five career runs, one sim-going run) and almost entirely unexposed over hurdles, while Lundy View's consistent form figures (6-7-7-8) suggest modest ability but orderly jumping.

watchPoints.text: Whermyrosemarygoes — if Cobden is allowed a completely uncontested lead into the first flight, the race may be over as a contest within a circuit; watch for any horse attempting to close the gap before the home turn.

King's Scholar — returning after 86 days off with Tom Hutsby claiming 10lb; if the break has left him ring-rusty over the first two hurdles, his prominent position becomes a liability rather than an asset.

Playful Fox — Harry Skelton may choose to push her closer than her natural hold-up style dictates given the small field and modest tempo; watch her position leaving the back straight as an indicator of Skelton's in-race read.

Devon Red — lightly raced and style unknown; any significant drift in the betting ring or a jockey instruction to jump off prominently could signal stable confidence and change the complexion of the race.

Lundy View — four consecutive finishes outside the frame on Good ground; monitor jumping at the early hurdles, as errors here on a tight track like Newton Abbot can create interference for those tracking behind.

races.name: Happy 80th Birthday John Lane Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: Sir Carnegie
runners_data.note: Strong record on Good ground with two wins and four places in 15 similar-going runs, and a hold-up style that is tailor-made for a contested-pace scenario over this 3m2f trip; 35 days since last run is acceptable and Mickey Bowen's stable is ticking over at 1/6 in the 14-day window.|
runners_data.comment: Sir Carnegie arrives here in decent nick, a winner twice in his last five starts including back-to-back victories, and he has experience over today's trip and going; the concern is that sixth last time out and a hefty 168 lb to carry.

runners_data.name: Great d'Ange
runners_data.note: A veteran front-runner (age 10) fitted with a tongue-tie/visor combination, boasting an exceptional 14/15 similar-going record including two recent Good-ground placed efforts over 26f; will force the pace alongside Limerick Leader and needs rivals to fold rather than fight back.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent in recent starts, Great d'Ange has back-to-back runner-up finishes to his name and has run over today's trip and going, giving him the experience needed here; winless in his last five, he nevertheless heads the ratings and looks the one to beat off 166 lb.

runners_data.name: Limerick Leader
runners_data.note: Remarkably consistent at placing — five consecutive top-three finishes — but the win has eluded this horse recently, suggesting it may lack the finishing kick to hold off challengers once the early duel with Great d'Ange takes its toll; blinkers fitted, trainer Nick Scholfield conditional yard going at 1/4 in the 14-day window.|
runners_data.comment: Limerick Leader has been a model of consistency, finishing placed in each of his last five starts — third last time out, second three starts back — and he has experience of today's going, while our rating puts him ahead of his official mark; the concern is that, winless in recent starts, he has yet to convert that reliability into a win.

runners_data.name: My Girl Katie
runners_data.note: Three wins on Good ground over 26f trips in the last 15 similar-going runs tells a clear story about this mare's suitability to today's conditions; Alix Balfe takes off 7lbs which is a meaningful allowance at this level, and Grace Harris's yard is firing at 2/16 recently — form string of 1213-1 underlines a lively winning attitude.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked fifth of six on our figures, My Girl Katie faces a stiff task on these ratings, though her recent form reads well with three wins in her last five starts; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 34 days off suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Honey I'm Good
runners_data.note: A prominent racer who will likely claim the position just behind the two front-runners; Good-ground record is modest at 1W from 10 similar runs and the tongue-tie is a retained piece of headgear to note, but at OR 83 it does need everything to go right positionally.|
runners_data.comment: Placed efforts of second and third in her last four starts highlight Honey I'm Good's consistent threat, she has run over today's trip and going, and a rating of 95 puts her among the strongest in this field — the concern is she remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Hardy Buck
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse placed further forward on the map only because the rear is over-subscribed in this race shape — in reality it will be ridden from off the pace, which means it needs a stronger-than-expected gallop to close the gap; headgear combination (tongue-piece and hood) retained, but OR 74 and a STYLE_FIT score of 0.91 temper any expectations in a shape where it cannot assume its natural position.|

races.paceDynamic: Great d'Ange and Limerick Leader are confirmed front-runners who will contest the lead from the off over this 3m2f trip at Newton Abbot, creating a genuine, honest gallop on Good ground. Great d'Ange has gate-to-tape form at this sort of trip and will not surrender the lead cheaply, while Limerick Leader's consistency in placing prominently means neither is likely to concede ground willingly early. The field contains more hold-up types than the positional map can accommodate: Hardy Buck is a genuine hold-up horse redistributed to midfield simply because the rear is already saturated, and in practice it is Great d'Ange and Limerick Leader who will secure the front positions, with Honey I'm Good slotting into a close-up prominent role behind them. A genuinely contested pace over 3m2f on Good ground strongly favours hold-up and off-the-pace profiles — horses who can travel within themselves, conserve energy through the early battle, and deliver a sustained late run when the pace-setters begin to weaken in the home straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Two Sustain, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Great d'Ange and Limerick Leader burn each other up setting a true gallop, leaving Sir Carnegie and My Girl Katie to pick up the pieces late.
scenarios.body: The contested early pace drains both front-runners in the final mile of a demanding 3m2f trip, opening the door for hold-up types to reel them in over the last two fences. Sir Carnegie's consistent Good-ground form and hold-up style suit this shape perfectly, while My Girl Katie's three wins on Good over similar trips mark her as a natural beneficiary.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Limerick Leader or Great d'Ange breaks cleanly and the other capitulates early, allowing one to control an uncontested rhythm.
scenarios.body: A single front-runner controlling pace on Good ground over this trip can set an energy-efficient gallop that blunts the closers' challenge. Great d'Ange's strong recent record in Good-ground events at this sort of trip makes it the more likely candidate to dominate if the duel fizzles early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Honey I'm Good tracks the front two at close quarters and the pace proves honest enough to gut the leaders without being truly scorching.
scenarios.body: Honey I'm Good sits handily just off the front pair throughout, conserving enough energy to grind past tired rivals in the closing stages without needing a sprint finish. Good-ground form is acceptable and the trip suits, though a higher official rating bar means it needs the pace to be exactly right.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Attrition, Any Survives
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is extreme, there are multiple jumping errors, or the race is effectively run as an endurance test that throws the form book out.
scenarios.body: A gruelling war of attrition over 3m2f can elevate a fresh or unexposed horse who simply stays on past felled rivals. Hardy Buck, though racing out of its natural deep hold-up position and carrying a style-fit discount, would benefit most from a race reduced to pure stamina in the closing stages.

watchPoints.text: Great d'Ange and Limerick Leader will almost certainly race hard against each other from flag-fall — watch whether either capitulates before halfway, as that determines whether this becomes a true contested gallop or a single-horse exhibition.
My Girl Katie is dropping to OR 92 with a 7lb claimer aboard — if Alix Balfe can restrain the mare smoothly off the pace, her three Good-ground wins over similar trips make her a serious late threat.

Hardy Buck's redistribution to midfield on the map does not reflect its true deep hold-up style — watch for Luke Scott going wider and further back than the map implies, which means it needs exceptional late pace to land a blow.

Limerick Leader has been placed 10 times in 15 similar-going runs without winning — watch for the horse to be headed approaching the last when the duel finally takes its toll, potentially flattening out.

Newton Abbot's 3m2f trip includes a significant number of fences in the back straight where mistakes by the front-runners could abruptly change the complexion of the race — jumping accuracy from Great d'Ange (age 10, tongue-tie/visor) is worth monitoring early.

races.name: Philip Wilson Memorial Novices' Limited Handicap Steeple Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Gore Point
runners_data.note: Comfortably the most in-form runner here with four wins from his last five starts on Good ground (5W10P on similar going across 15 runs), and Anthony Honeyball's 6yo is clearly suited to this trip range; a natural hold-up horse who will rely on Sam Twiston-Davies delivering him late, 40 days since last run is no concern given the freshness of his record.
runners_data.comment: Gore Point arrives in fine form with three wins in his last five starts, including back-to-back victories, and has experience of both today's trip and going; the main concern is that 40 days off the track leaves his sharpness to be proven.

runners_data.name: Cobbler's Boy
runners_data.note: Sarah-Jayne Davies's 6yo carries a positive T14 yard flag (0/3 runners but active) and has a win and a place on similar going (2W3P from 5), though his natural instinct is to race from the rear — in a four-runner field where multiple horses want the same late ground, he risks getting boxed in or racing without clear air.
runners_data.comment: Cobbler's Boy advertises strong claims on the back of a win three starts back and a second two starts back, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; the concern is a below-par seventh last time out after a 62-day absence that may have left him short of peak fitness.

runners_data.name: Ice Jet
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's 4yo has won three of his last four chase starts and is in exceptional form, but he is a hold-up type by nature being asked to fulfil the front-runner's role here because no confirmed pacemaker exists — the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.80 is real, and the key question is whether Harry Skelton can settle him comfortably enough on the lead to preserve a finish; his T14 record of 4/14 runners is the standout trainer stat in the race.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in his last five starts, a runner-up two starts back, and a return to a trip and going he has experience of all combine to make Ice Jet an appealing proposition carrying 153 lb fresh from a 29-day break.

runners_data.name: Hooper
runners_data.note: The veteran 10yo from the Nigel & Willy Twiston-Davies yard has no wins on Good ground across a 12-run sample on similar surfaces (0W6P), and while his hold-up style suits a race with a lone front-runner, the ceiling on his OR of 100 and the amateur jockey (7lb claim) make this a hope-for-the-best scenario; placed form exists but winning form does not on this going type.
runners_data.comment: Hooper has run over today's trip and going before and, rated 121 against just three rivals, makes a compelling case as the most dangerous threat in this field; the concern is that he has been winless in his last five starts, with a second two runs back sandwiched between less encouraging efforts.

races.paceDynamic: Ice Jet is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this four-runner field, and with no genuine front-runner to push him, Harry Skelton can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over 2m½f on Good turf at Newton Abbot — a track that rewards jumping fluency and positional security. Gore Point is a natural hold-up horse with strong recent form, likely to be held up off the pace by Sam Twiston-Davies and produce his challenge in the home straight. Cobbler's Boy and Hooper are both genuine hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning the rear of this small field will be somewhat congested with closers rather than true pressing types. This race shape — a lone pace-setter controlling an uncontested, unhurried gallop — strongly favours Ice Jet if he can translate his prominent-type jump form to the lead role, but equally sets up a patient hold-up horse like Gore Point who can pounce on a potentially flat-finishing front-runner in the final stages; the redistribution of Cobbler's Boy and Hooper out of their natural hold-up positions further compresses the field's tactical range, ultimately making this a race where a sound jumper relaxed in front, or a well-timed closer off a genuine solo lead, is best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ice Jet Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Ice Jet settles into a comfortable lead and jumps cleanly throughout, dictating the tempo with no rival pressing him.
scenarios.body: Harry Skelton gives Ice Jet an uncontested lead and controls the fractions on Good ground, and Ice Jet's strong recent winning sequence (three wins from four runs) suggests the class to sustain it.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Gore Point Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Ice Jet sets only a moderate gallop and ties up approaching the last, allowing Gore Point to reel him in.
scenarios.body: Sam Twiston-Davies settles Gore Point in last or second-last, conserving energy on a Good surface that suits him (11 from 15 on similar going), and a powerful late run from the 6yo who has won four of his last five lands the prize.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Cobbler's Boy Delivers Quietly
scenarios.trigger: If the race is truly sedate early and Cobbler's Boy, despite being displaced from his natural hold-up position, tracks into contention and finds a clear run from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Sarah-Jayne Davies's runner has a win and a place at this trip and going, and if the redistribution effect is minimised by a very slow pace, his 2W3P record on similar going gives him a live outsider chance.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hooper Causes Upset
scenarios.trigger: If the race falls apart through jumping errors or a collapse by Ice Jet, and Hooper's veteran tactical nous allows him to pick through the wreckage.
scenarios.body: Hooper has never won on similar going (0W6P on Good) and is a decade-old horse carrying the lowest OR in the field, so this scenario requires near-chaos; his jockey's claim may help offset the weight but the form evidence is weak.

watchPoints.text: Ice Jet's jumping under pressure — if he makes a significant error at any of the early fences on the far side, the uncontested lead evaporates and Gore Point will be perfectly placed to capitalise.

Cobbler's Boy and Hooper are both natural hold-up horses sharing the same rear quarter of a four-runner field; watch for crowding or a lack of daylight approaching the final two fences, which could cost either runner a clean run.

Ice Jet's STYLE_FIT score (0.80) flags genuine uncertainty about whether he will settle on the lead — if Skelton cannot switch him off in the early stages, over-racing on Good ground could see him flat and vulnerable at the last.

Gore Point's 40-day absence is on the shorter side for a jumper, but his five-run winning streak and strong sim-going record (11/15) suggest he returns ready; watch his jumping in the first half of the race as any hesitancy would undermine the hold-up plan in a small field.

races.name: Torbay Weekly Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Lakefield Flyer
runners_data.note: Won over 20f on Good going 27 days ago with Liam Harrison aboard; front-runner who should lead from the off and whose recent course-and-distance form (14 runs on similar going, 2 wins 6 places) makes him genuinely dangerous if allowed to control tempo rather than being pressed relentlessly by rivals.
runners_data.comment: Lakefield Flyer showed his best when winning three starts back and was third two starts back, giving him the strongest recent profile in this field. He has run over today's trip and going, returns after 27 days, and our rating of 103 marks him as the one to beat despite a hefty 168 lb burden.

runners_data.name: Time Interval
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton takes the ride for an in-form Dan Skelton yard (4/14 last 14 days) but this horse has been off 125 days and his form reads 6567P — he may lack the sharpness to sustain a front-running effort over this stamina-testing trip and could fade if committed to early pace.

runners_data.name: Hillsin
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse for Alan Jones, James Turner (5lb claimer) riding; three wins on similar going from 15 runs and won over 18f on Good — the strong pace suits his style perfectly and his fresh legs (79 days off) may give him an end-of-race advantage if he can find a clear run.
runners_data.comment: Hillsin landed a win in his last five starts and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with our rating of 97 suggesting he arrives as a leading threat on a fair mark; the key concern is a troubled recent run of pulled-up efforts and 79 days off the track.

runners_data.name: Son Of Hypnos
runners_data.note: Hold-up type from Ryan Chapman's yard ridden by 7lb claimer Jack Stenhouse; headgear (tv) on and only one place from nine runs on similar going suggests he finds these conditions tough, and the weight concession from the claimer is offset by limited recent form.
runners_data.comment: Son Of Hypnos has run over today's trip and going, arrives here fresh on 34 days' rest, and our rating of 97 marks him out as a genuine danger in this field; yet to score in his last five starts, and that pulled-up effort further back remains the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Electric Eddy
runners_data.note: Sam Twiston-Davies partners this genuine hold-up horse for the family yard; trainer is 0/8 in the last 14 days which is a concern, but 13 runs on similar going (one win, seven places) shows he handles conditions and his style suits a strongly-run race well.
runners_data.comment: Electric Eddy arrives 46 days since his last run and yet to win in his last five starts, though a third three starts back shows he can hit the frame; the question is whether 161 lb lets him build on that.

runners_data.name: Uncle Remus
runners_data.note: Five-year-old from Henrietta Knight's yard with Sean Bowen aboard; his natural game is to come from well off the pace but the congested field of hold-up horses means he'll likely be racing closer than ideal, softening the potency of his finish — the style displacement is a real handicap here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Uncle Remus does show a third three starts back that hints at better, and his going experience is a clear asset under his 159 lb burden; the concern is that his two most recent outings have been well below that level.

runners_data.name: Ugo Bingo
runners_data.note: Turf-specialist for Joe Tizzard, Brendan Powell up; no wins from nine runs on similar going flags a consistency issue, and like several others in this field he is a genuine hold-up horse who will find himself racing further forward than he'd choose, blunting his chance of hitting the line fresh.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Ugo Bingo at least shows experience over today's trip and going, though 158 lb is a stern burden and a ranking of sixth from ten leaves him with plenty to find against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Saucats
runners_data.note: Front-runner wearing headgear (tp) for Joe Tickle, 13 runs on similar going with a win and six places — his recent form sequence (255123) shows genuine consistency and he could be the horse who best mixes pace-setting with stamina if the other two leaders crack first.
runners_data.comment: Ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Saucats is hard to fancy at the weights, but he does arrive in fair nick — third last time out, a winner three starts back — and has experience of today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Man Oh Man
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing a hood for D Summersby, Bryan Carver rides; his true style is to come from deep but with the rear of the field crowded with similar types he'll be forced closer, and his record shows no wins from similar going across 15 attempts — context for modest expectations.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Man Oh Man faces a stiff ask here; that said, he has run over today's trip and going before, and a second two starts back shows he retains ability when conditions align.

runners_data.name: Hawa Jumeirah
runners_data.note: Five-year-old filly from Helen Nelmes, wearing a hood; she's a natural hold-up horse who will face the same positional squeeze as several rivals, having to race further forward than suits her; 11 runs on similar going with one win shows she handles conditions but her best races come when allowed to close freely.
runners_data.comment: Hawa Jumeirah arrives on the back of consecutive thirds and has run over today's trip and going, though he remains winless in his last five starts and a stiff 149 lb burden makes this a tough ask from seventh in the ratings.

runners_data.name: Mi Sueno
runners_data.note: Prominent racer wearing a hood for Nick Scholfield's yard (1/4 T14), Harry Reed up; won over 18f on Good and his style sits more naturally in the prominent bracket, meaning he avoids the redistribution problem — a Good-ground performer who is better suited to this shape than his low OR of 78 might suggest.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Mi Sueno faces a stiff ask, and four defeats before his latest win — which included a pulled up — do little to inspire confidence; that said, he returns with experience of today's trip and going, and his recent victory at least confirms he retains ability.

races.paceDynamic: Lakefield Flyer, Time Interval, and Saucats are all confirmed front-runners in an 11-runner field, guaranteeing a strong gallop from the outset over 2m2½f on Good turf at Newton Abbot — a track that already tests stamina through its undulations and tight turns. With three horses actively contesting for the lead, the pace will be genuine and sustained, burning off any false-run comfort and placing a heavy premium on jumping cleanly and travelling economically through the early stages. This race shape strongly favours hold-up and prominent horses with proven stamina at this trip — runners who can settle behind the pace battle, conserve energy, and arrive with a clean run in the straight. The field contains more hold-up types than the positional map can accommodate at the rear: Uncle Remus, Ugo Bingo, Man Oh Man, and Hawa Jumeirah are all true come-from-behind horses who will be forced to race closer to the pace than is natural to them, meaning Hillsin and Electric Eddy — genuine hold-up types with stamina profiles that suit a strongly-run race — are best positioned to exploit the shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War Burns Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Lakefield Flyer, Time Interval, and Saucats push each other through a genuinely fierce gallop and fail to conserve enough for the finish.
scenarios.body: The three front-runners exhaust each other setting a punishing tempo, leaving the race wide open for hold-up horses to pick up the pieces in the straight; stamina and a clean jump at the last become decisive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three front-runners — most likely Lakefield Flyer given course/going profile and recent win — establishes a clear lead while the others settle just off.
scenarios.body: A controlled but honest gallop allows the leader to dictate rhythm and keep enough in reserve; runners who travelled prominently without expending energy scrapping for position arrive with the best chance.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace battle blows up early and runners sitting just off the pace in a handy prominent position avoid the worst of the scrapping.
scenarios.body: Horses who break well and slot in behind the leaders without burning energy fighting for front rank find themselves perfectly placed as the field concertinas turning for home; a moderate sprint to the line favours tactical versatility.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is truly relentless and all runners prominent or closer are weakening, allowing deep hold-up horses to motor through beaten rivals.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires the true closers — Hillsin and Son Of Hypnos — to find a clear passage late, which is harder at a tight track like Newton Abbot; redistributed hold-up types like Uncle Remus and Hawa Jumeirah are compromised by racing out of role and receive a meaningful discount here.

watchPoints.text: Watch the early scrapping between Lakefield Flyer, Time Interval, and Saucats — if all three press hard from the first hurdle, the pace will be punishing and their chance of finishing could evaporate dramatically before the second circuit.

Hillsin (79 days off, 5lb claimer James Turner) is worth monitoring in the market: if fresh and well enough to produce his best, his hold-up style is the ideal fit for this shape, but the combination of a long absence and a claiming rider introduces meaningful uncertainty.

Time Interval's 125-day absence for Dan Skelton — despite the yard being in form — is a serious flag; front-runners returning from a break rarely handle the extra energy cost of setting a strong gallop and could drop out suddenly.

Mi Sueno's hood and prominent style place him in the best tactical position among the lower-rated horses — if the pace war destroys the leaders, he could inherit a clear run without having used up energy fighting for position.

The cluster of hold-up horses (Uncle Remus, Ugo Bingo, Man Oh Man, Hawa Jumeirah) all racing out of natural position means Newton Abbot's tight home turn could cause significant traffic issues — runners drawn wide or with late-moving jockeys face extra risk of being stopped in their run.

races.name: Aubrey Loze Memorial Handicap Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Soul Icon
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old prominent racer who handles good ground well and has a solid record in this type of staying handicap hurdle; amateur rider Mr Hugo Hunt claims 7lb which is a significant weight aid, and trainer Keiran Burke has a live runner here (1 from 5 in 14 days); tailed off last time but has claims at this trip on good ground based on earlier form, and the front-running pace suits a horse who likes to travel into a gallop.
runners_data.comment: Soul Icon has been frustratingly consistent without a win in his last five starts, though a bring-down and an unseating unseat the picture somewhat; he has run over today's trip and going, carries a hefty 168 lb, yet our rating of 146 marks him as the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Zillow
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden takes the mount for Faye Bramley and that jockey booking is the headline here; a genuine hold-up type who needs things to go wrong for others, and his recent string of poor efforts (F00-7P) suggests this is a revival job — good ground is fine but the form is a significant concern and he would need the race to collapse in his favour.
runners_data.comment: Zillow has experience of today's going and comes here on a quick enough turnaround at 27 days, with our rating of 133 marking him out as a leading player in this field; the concern is a winless recent run of five starts that includes a fall and a pull-up, leaving his current form hard to assess.

runners_data.name: American Sniper
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with two wins on good ground and strong course form at Newton Abbot; David Pipe has had no runners in 14 days which is neutral, and the 55-day absence needs noting, but this horse's style is exactly what it is — he will make the running and his stamina over 2m5½f is proven; the danger is Handlethekettle fighting him for the lead.
runners_data.comment: American Sniper won one start back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a serious threat at the head of the market; the main concern is that he returns after a 55-day absence and faces a stiff weight of 156 lb.

runners_data.name: Handlethekettle
runners_data.note: The most striking entry here — four wins from seven on good ground, excellent front-running record, and a high-class profile, but he returns from 411 days off with Jamie Snowden's stable bang in form (3 from 4, 14 days); if he's fit enough to reproduce his best he could prove very hard to beat from the front, but the layoff is a genuine fitness question that this trip will ruthlessly expose.
runners_data.comment: Handlethekettle arrives on the back of three wins in his last four starts, including back-to-back victories, and has experience of today's going, but 411 days off the track is the significant unknown for this progressive gelding carrying 155 lb.

runners_data.name: Kitty Foyle
runners_data.note: Won over 2m4f on good ground and was a solid second last time over this sort of distance; Harry Reed rides, and the pattern of her form — placed regularly on good ground at 2m-plus — fits this race shape well; a natural hold-up horse who will be produced late, but in a truly run race she has the stamina profile to finish off the leaders strongly.
runners_data.comment: Placed in four of her last five starts, including a win one start back and a second last time out, Kitty Foyle arrives fit enough after 45 days off and has going experience to call upon, though her burden of 154 lb and a ranking of fifth of eight temper expectations.

runners_data.name: Morning Mayhem
runners_data.note: Nick Scholfield's five-year-old has a win and two thirds at track trips around 2m-2m2f on good ground; his natural style is to hold up and wait, but the abundance of hold-up types in this field means Kielan Woods will need to adapt his positioning — racing out of his preferred role will test his tactical versatility, and the step up to 2m5½f is a query for a horse whose best form sits at shorter.
runners_data.comment: Morning Mayhem has a win among his last five starts but has finished fourth twice since, and at 152 lb he faces a stiff weight assignment; he has run over today's going before and returns after a 35-day break with something to prove.

runners_data.name: Letterston Lily
runners_data.note: Mickey Bowen saddles his daughter's mount and Letterston Lily won over 2m on good ground but her last three have been disappointing; she is a hold-up type by instinct but this crowded rear-of-field shapes her race unfavourably — the form line includes an 8th and an 11th in her most recent starts, and until she recaptures her winning form the hold-up dependency is a real tactical liability.
runners_data.comment: Eighth last time out makes Letterston Lily hard to fancy here, ranked seventh of eight on our figures, and 150 lb is a stiff burden; she has run over today's trip and going, and that win the start before at least shows she retains ability on her day.

runners_data.name: Supreme Yeats
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's ten-year-old has an outstanding recent record — four wins from his last five including back-to-back successes over 2m2f-2m2f on good ground — and Harry Skelton will find a position regardless of nominal map placement; a true hold-up horse who needs a strong pace to aim at, and this race delivers exactly that, making him the most dangerous of the deeper-tracked horses despite his age.
runners_data.comment: Supreme Yeats has winning form in his recent starts, including a win last time out, and has run over today's trip and going before, but he ranks last on our figures in this field and a 57-day absence gives pause for thought.

races.paceDynamic: American Sniper and Handlethekettle are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off, creating an honest, competitive gallop over 2m5½f on good ground at Newton Abbot. American Sniper has course experience and has won from the front on good ground, while Handlethekettle returns from 411 days off but has a strong record of setting and sustaining his own pace. With two genuine pace horses fighting for the lead across a stamina-testing trip, the gallop is unlikely to be slow — this is a true-run race that will stretch the field and put a premium on relentless galloping ability and jumping efficiency over finishing speed. This shape favours prominent-to-held-up horses with genuine stamina who can travel comfortably into a strong pace and pick off a tiring leader late — Soul Icon and Kitty Foyle, tracking at or just off the pace, are best positioned to exploit it. Morning Mayhem, Letterston Lily and Supreme Yeats are all genuine hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map because the field holds more hold-up horses than the race shape can absorb at the rear; of these, Supreme Yeats (Harry Skelton) and Kitty Foyle are most likely to actually secure a useful position given jockey quality and race craft.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Tracker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If American Sniper and Handlethekettle burn each other up over the first mile and the honest gallop suits a prominent tracker who jumps cleanly and stays on strongly.
scenarios.body: The two leaders set a genuine pace that depletes them in the closing stages, handing the advantage to a horse sitting just behind in a rhythm — Soul Icon or Kitty Foyle are ideally positioned to exploit the gap as the front pair tire. This is the dominant shape given confirmed dual pace and a stamina trip that punishes front-runners who fought for position early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Handlethekettle (or American Sniper) establishes a clear lead early and the other drops away, allowing one to bowl along at a controlled tempo.
scenarios.body: A sole leader setting its own rhythm over 2m5½f on good ground can prove very hard to peg back if the pace is measured rather than frenetic — Handlethekettle's record of winning from the front on good ground makes this a genuine threat, particularly on his return to form. American Sniper likewise has the course experience and front-running CV to capitalise if Handlethekettle fails to recover race fitness after his long layoff.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly furious and the entire field is stretched, allowing a genuinely patient closer to pick up the pieces in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: Supreme Yeats has an excellent recent record on good ground over staying trips and Harry Skelton will find cover regardless of where the map places him — if the gallop is truly strong, his stamina profile suits a sustained late challenge. Kitty Foyle, who won over this sort of trip at a similar track, also has the engine to finish powerfully if gaps appear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scrambles The Pack
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fallers, mistakes or a riderless horse disrupts the rhythm and the race shape collapses into an untidy, stop-start affair.
scenarios.body: A messy race with jumping errors from front-runners would scramble normal pace dynamics and open the door to a horse with a clean round of jumping regardless of position — Zillow, though badly out of form, is ridden by Harry Cobden and could sneak into contention if chaos clears his path. Morning Mayhem, sharp enough to slot into a gap if the race fragments, is also worth noting.

watchPoints.text: Handlethekettle's fitness after 411 days off is the single biggest variable in this race — if he fires fresh he may not be caught, but if he blows up from setting the pace, the entire race shape shifts in favour of the trackers.

American Sniper and Handlethekettle will contest the early lead and if neither concedes, the pace could become genuinely brutal — watch for either horse folding dramatically from 3 out, which would significantly boost Soul Icon and Kitty Foyle.

Supreme Yeats (Harry Skelton) is a natural closer who has won four of his last five on good ground at staying trips — his jockey will not be constrained by a map position and he should be expected to work forward from early on; do not underestimate him in a truly run race.
Zillow's booking of Harry Cobden is unexplained by the form book and worth monitoring in market moves — if there is stable confidence behind the ride it would be the biggest plot twist in the race.

Good ground is confirmed across all Newton Abbot races today and is consistent throughout the card — no horse has a meaningful going concern, which means form on similar conditions is a reliable guide and the stamina test at 2m5½f will be genuine.

races.name: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Charlus
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's hold-up runner wearing headgear, returning 35 days after a modest run; similar-going record is unimpressive (0W1P in 14 qualifying runs) and needs traffic to open up in a small field, which is far from guaranteed.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Charlus nevertheless heads this field on ratings and has run over today's trip and going, giving connections a solid platform; the 168 lb burden is the one note of caution, but 35 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh and ready.

runners_data.name: Mojito Des Mottes
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden takes the ride on this four-year-old for Ben Pauling, a natural prominent racer with solid good-ground form (0W2P in 5 runs at similar going); the contested gallop set by the two front-runners plays directly to his tracking style and he has placed at this distance and trip configuration before.|
runners_data.comment: Pulled up last time out is the blunt entry point here — Mojito Des Mottes has been winless in his last five starts, and our rating ranks him fifth of six runners, making him hard to fancy despite previous placed efforts and experience over today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Max Of Stars
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with an excellent good-ground record (3W7P in 15 qualifying runs), freshened up on just 17 days' rest; Sam Twiston-Davies aboard gives him every chance to dictate if Sayva doesn't dominate, though a duel from flag-fall will drain his reserves.|
runners_data.comment: A winner four starts back, Max Of Stars arrives here on the back of a third three starts back and brings strong claims on a rating of 120; the main concern is her unseated-rider blot two starts back.

runners_data.name: Sayva
runners_data.note: Jonjo & A.J. O'Neill's front-runner faces a significant fitness question after 239 days off the track, and his best form has come over further on softer; on quick ground over 2m1f fresh, his stamina and sharpness are genuine concerns even if he naturally wants to lead.|
runners_data.comment: Sayva shapes as a leading threat on our rating of 123, and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but he arrives winless in his last four starts and a 239-day absence is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Arctic Voyage
runners_data.note: Michael Blake's consistent four-year-old boasts an impressive strike rate at similar going (3W5P in 15 runs) and won over today's distance and going type; races from hold-up, so benefits if the contested pace is strong enough to set up a late run, and Harry Reed has only one other ride for the trainer in recent days — this looks a live chance.|
runners_data.comment: Arctic Voyage arrives on the back of three wins in his last five starts, including a victory last time out, and has experience of today's trip and conditions — a potent profile that makes him a leading danger here; the main concern is whether 50 days off the track has left him short of peak sharpness.

runners_data.name: Lunar Orbit
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton rides this Dan Skelton-trained four-year-old who is a genuine hold-up type by style, but with Charlus and Arctic Voyage also wanting the rear, he is unlikely to find his natural position and is mapped to midfield as a result — his STYLE_FIT score of 0.93 reflects he will be racing out of role, which tempers confidence despite a solid hurdles record on soft ground.|
runners_data.comment: Lunar Orbit is hard to fancy ranked last on our figures and returning from a 198-day absence carrying 151 lb, though he has winning form two starts back and experience over today's trip and going to his name.

races.paceDynamic: Sayva and Max Of Stars are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over 2m1f on good ground at Newton Abbot, creating a genuinely contested, honest gallop rather than a dawdle. With two pace horses locking horns early, the race is likely to be run at a consistent tempo throughout, which typically stretches the field and tests stamina reserves in the closing stages. Charlus, Arctic Voyage, and Lunar Orbit all carry hold-up profiles, but the field holds more hold-up types than can realistically fill those rear positions — Lunar Orbit in particular is a genuine hold-up horse who may struggle to settle as far back as desired given the compression of types at the rear. This race shape — honest pace set by duelling front-runners over a sound surface — strongly favours horses with a prominent or close-tracking style who can travel into the race without expending energy early, making Mojito Des Mottes the profile that fits most naturally off the contested gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Tracker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Sayva and Max Of Stars fight for the lead and set a true gallop, allowing a close tracker to pounce
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other up through the early and middle stages, leaving a horse travelling smoothly just off the pace ideally placed to take over approaching the last. A prominent profile with good hurdles form on good ground is perfectly suited to capitalise on the pace collapse.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners settles into a clear lead without a sustained battle for supremacy
scenarios.body: Max Of Stars in particular has strong good-ground form and if Sayva concedes the lead early, the sole pace-setter could dictate a controlled gallop and prove hard to reel in. A horse able to dictate its own rhythm without burning fuel tends to find reserves late in handicap company at this trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is truly scorching and the front-runners tie each other up, leaving the hold-up horses with ground to make up from the home turn
scenarios.body: Charlus and Arctic Voyage would be the primary beneficiaries if the race falls apart at the front, swooping late as fatigued leaders capitulate. However, this scenario requires genuine burn-out from the leaders and hold-up types getting a clear run — both conditions are uncertain in a six-runner field on good ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Modest Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If neither front-runner commits fully and the race devolves into a muddling, falsely-run contest
scenarios.body: A stop-start pace would scramble the form book and create chaos at the business end, potentially favouring fresh legs or a horse with a late turn of foot. This is the least likely outcome given both Sayva and Max Of Stars have demonstrated front-running tendencies, making a truly slow gallop almost implausible.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Sayva shows any signs of fitness concerns after 239 days off — if she jumps sluggishly or is immediately outpaced by Max Of Stars, the lone-leader scenario (Scenario B) flips from unlikely to dominant very quickly.

Arctic Voyage's good-ground strike rate (3W in 15 similar-going runs) makes her a serious threat if the front-runners burn each other out; monitor how quickly Harry Reed moves her into contention after the final bend.

Lunar Orbit is squeezed into a midfield map position but is a true hold-up horse — in a six-runner race there is simply nowhere to hide, and if he over-races chasing a contested pace his chance may be compromised before the straight.

Max Of Stars has an OR of 115 and good-ground form, but his recent run at a shorter trip (10f) and a contested pace duel with Sayva could leave him exposed in the final 2f if he has burned his turbo early.

Mojito Des Mottes pulled up on his most recent start — Harry Cobden's handling of that run and whether there were any post-race concerns is worth monitoring; if he returns to his earlier placed form over 2m on good ground, the prominent-tracking profile suits this race shape exactly.
